title: Change minlength/maxlength behavior around linebreaks and code points

labels.name: do not merge yet
labels.description: Pull request must not be merged per rationale in comment

body:
As discussed in #1467, the current situation around these attributes is
not very interoperable in two ways:
- Some browsers count line breaks as two characters (per the spec),
  others as one character.
- Some browsers count code units (per the spec), others code points,
  others grapheme clusters.

Per discussions, this updates minlength and maxlength, as well as
textarea's textLength property, to count line breaks as one character
and to count code points. We believe this is the most developer-friendly
approach. Notably the choice of code points aligns with the pattern=""
attribute.

Fixes #1467.

---

Note that per 

I would like implementer buy-in across the board here to make sure we are aligned again, instead of just moving from the spec saying one thing most implementers don't follow, to another thing most implementers don't follow.

Here is the compat matrix (largely copied from @tkent-google's table in #1467). For maxlength/minlength

|  | Google Chrome | WebKit | Firefox | Edge, IE | Old spec | New spec |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A linebreak | 2 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 1 |
| Non-BMP character | 2 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 1 |
| Letter + combining char | 2 | 1 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 |

So this would require:
- Chrome:
  - Move from code units to code points
  - Change linebreaks from 2 to 1 character
- WebKit:
  - Move from grapheme clusters to code points
  - Change linebreaks from 2 to 1 character
- Firefox:
  - Move from code units to code points
- Edge: no change

@tkent-google seems OK with the change, per https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/1467#issuecomment-231132094. @smaug----, would you be able to help direct this question appropriately for Gecko?

I am especially interested in Apple's perspective, since their choice of grapheme clusters is arguably more user-friendly (although maybe devs would be surprised). @rniwa, since you previously engaged in https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=120030, do you think moving to code points would be OK? Darin's conclusion in that bug was

> Anyway, we should match the standard, but it’s nuts that the standard does not consider actual end user concepts of string length and instead concentrates on internals in this way.

Hopefully matching the standard is still a priority here, and using code points instead of code units softens the blow a bit?
